editorial:
Imagine living in a tiny basement with your whole family, struggling just to get free Wi-Fi. That is where you meet the Kim family. They are smart and scrappy, but they have no jobs. When the son gets a chance to tutor a girl for a rich family, he slowly helps his parents and sister trick their way into working for the wealthy Parks. It starts off like a funny heist movie where you are rooting for the underdogs to make some easy money. The vibe is light and clever, making you feel like you are in on a big secret as the Kims move into the Parks' glamorous home.

Once you think you know where the story is going, a huge twist flips everything upside down. The acting is top-notch, and the way the story speeds up in the second half will leave you breathless. You will love how it balances laughs with genuine tension. While some parts get pretty dark and stressful, the pacing is perfect. If you enjoy stories about class struggles or movies that keep you guessing until the very last minute, you absolutely need to see this one.
endingExplained: The movie ends in a violent clash at a birthday party. Ki-taek kills Mr. Park after feeling disgusted by his reaction to a bad smell. Ki-taek then hides in the secret basement of the house for years. His son, Ki-woo, eventually writes a letter promising to make enough money to buy the house one day so his father can finally walk out into the sunlight, though it is likely just a dream.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves smart plots and unexpected twists.
